chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, who said:

I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding Al-Nabeez? For Abu Maryam drinks it and claims that you ordered him to drink it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Maryam spoke the truth. He asked me about Al-Nabeez, so I informed him that it is permissible, and he did not ask me about the intoxicant.'

He said, then he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the intoxicant, I did not practice dissimulation (taqiyyah) regarding it for anyone, neither authority nor anyone else.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is forbidden.'
So the man said to him (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! This Al-Nabeez which you permitted Abu Maryam to drink, what is it?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for my father (peace be upon him), he used to order the servant to bring a cup, put raisins in it, and wash it with a clean washing. Then he put it in a vessel, then poured over it water three or four times its amount. Then he left it at night and drank it during the day, and left it in the morning and drank it in the evening. And he used to order the servant to wash the vessel every three days, lest it become sour. So if you want Al-Nabeez, this is Al-Nabeez.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A drink made by soaking raisins (or other fruits) in water
key_terms.الْغَلَب: To become sour or fermented to the point of being considered intoxicating/khamr

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Nabeez and Khamr, and how is Nabeez prepared to remain permissible?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic distinction between *nabidh* and *khamr* by detailing Imam al-Sadiq’s specific preparation method, which prevents fermentation through controlled water ratios and daily vessel cleaning. It reinforces the Shia legal principle of *tadarruj* (gradual prohibition) and the rule that 'what intoxicates in large quantities is forbidden in small quantities,' while highlighting the practical necessity of preventing *khamr* (souring) to maintain permissibility. This narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding how early Shia scholars applied prophetic traditions to daily consumption practices.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr who said,

‘I heard a man and he was saying to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding Al-Nabeez, for Abu Maryam is drinking it and he is claiming that youasws ordered him with drinking it?’ So heasws said: ‘Abu Maryam spoke the truth. He asked measws about Al-Nabeez, so Iasws informed him that it is Permissible, and he did not ask me about the intoxicant’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the intoxicants, there is no dissimulation in it for anyone, neither from the authorities nor someone else. Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is Prohibited, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates so a little of it is Prohibited’.
So the man said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! This Al-Nabeez which youasws are permitting for Abu Maryam with regards to drinking it, which thing is it?’

So heasws said: ‘As for myasws fatherasws, heasws had ordered the servant, so he came with a cup, and heasws made raisins to be in it, and washed it with a washing, clean. Then heasws made it to be in a vessel, then poured water over it the like of three or four times of it. Then heasws made it at night and heasws would drink it at daytime, and heasws made it at daytime and heasws would drink it in the evening. And heasws used to order the servant with washing the vessel every three days, perhaps it would have stained. Thus, if you all are wanting Al-Nabeez, so this is Al-Nabeez’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Hanan ibn Sadir who has said the following:

“I once heard a man who asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘What do you say about al-Nabidh? Abu Maryam drinks it and he thinks that you have commanded him to drink. ’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Abu Maryam has spoken the truth. He asked me about al-Nabidh but not about intoxicating liquor.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘Intoxicating liquor is as such that one must not even seek Taqiyah (caution because of fear) before al-Sultan or others. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “Intoxicating liquor is unlawful and whatever is intoxicating in large quantity is unlawful in small quantity also.’”
The man then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, what is al-Nabidh which you allowed abu Maryam to use?’

He (the Imam) said, ‘My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would order the servant to bring a bowl and place raisins in it; wash them clean, place it in a bowl then pour on it three or four times as much water. Then keep it overnight to drink it in the morning and place it in a bowl in the morning to drink it in the evening. He (the Imam) commanded the servant to wash the bowl after every three days to remove the stain, if it had formed. If you want al-Nabidh, this is al-Nabidh.’”
